families.covers: MA systems, ADX/DMI, Ichimoku, SuperTrend, Aroon, Vortex
families.guardrail: Cap highly correlated MA indicators as one sub-group

families.covers: RSI, MACD, Stochastic, CCI, ROC, TSI, TRIX
families.guardrail: Do not count every oscillator as an independent vote

families.covers: Volume, OBV, CMF, A/D, MFI, PVT, VWMA
families.guardrail: Price direction must accompany volume expansion

families.covers: ATR, Bands Width, CHOP, HV, SD, SE
families.guardrail: Risk output may be neutral directionally

families.covers: Pivots, profiles, fractals, Zig Zag, channels
families.guardrail: Use confirmed levels; Zig Zag can repaint

score_scale.label: Neutral / Non-directional
score_scale.interpretation: No confirmed direction or risk-only metric

indicators.rule: Rising 5-bar A/D confirms accumulation; falling confirms distribution; prioritize bullish/bearish divergence versus price.
Rising ASI and break above its prior swing high is bullish; falling ASI and support break is bearish.

indicators.parameters: Daily advances minus declines; optional 20-day MA
indicators.rule: Rising A/D line confirms broad participation; index rising while A/D falls is bearish divergence.
Close above a rising ALMA is bullish; close below a falling ALMA is bearish.
Aroon Up >70 and above Down is bullish; Down >70 and above Up is bearish; both low suggests consolidation.
ADX <20 weak; 20-25 developing; >25 trending. Direction comes from +DI versus -DI; favor a rising ADX.
Use as a reference only. Close above is mildly positive but not a standalone buy signal.
Non-directional. Use for risk and position sizing; typical stop distance 1.5-2.0 ATR adjusted to support and timeframe.
Above zero is bullish momentum; below zero bearish; use zero-line crosses or twin-peak patterns with trend confirmation.
Above zero indicates buyer dominance; below zero seller dominance; divergence strengthens the signal.
Lower/upper touches are not automatic trades. Use re-entry for mean reversion or high-volume band break for continuation.
<0 below lower band; >1 above upper band. Cross back inside can confirm reversal; >1 with volume can confirm breakout.
Historically low width signals a squeeze; expansion signals a volatility move. Obtain direction from price breakout.
Above 0 accumulation; below 0 distribution. +/-0.05 filters noise; +/-0.10 is stronger. Prefer sustained readings.
Above zero or bullish cross indicates improving money flow; below zero or bearish cross indicates deterioration.
Rising indicates range expansion and falling contraction; it does not determine direction.
Bullish when price closes above the upper/short-position stop structure; bearish below lower/long-position stop. Confirm platform line names.
Above zero positive and below zero negative; +/-50 are strong/extreme. Use crosses back through extremes for reversal confirmation.
Use EMA slope/angle classification. Trend colors support directional entries; neutral colors indicate choppy conditions.
Above 61.8 is choppy; below 38.2 is trending. Use another indicator to determine direction.
Above +100 often confirms bullish momentum; below -100 bearish. Mean-reversion signal requires crossing back through the threshold.
Below 20/10 is oversold/extreme and above 80/90 overbought/extreme; require price reversal confirmation.
Best on weekly/monthly charts. Turning upward from below zero is bullish; negative alone is not a sell.

indicators.parameters: 20-60 periods of log returns versus named benchmark
indicators.rule: Near +1 moves together; near 0 weak relation; near -1 inverse. Use for portfolio risk, not trend direction.
Above +0.7 high positive; -0.3 to +0.3 low; below -0.7 strong inverse. No standalone buy/sell.
Use cycle peaks and troughs after trend removal; zero-line position alone is not a trade signal.
+DI above -DI is bullish and reverse bearish; strongest when ADX is rising and above 25.
Close above prior upper channel is bullish breakout; below prior lower channel bearish. Exclude current bar from channel.
Close above a rising DEMA is bullish; below a falling DEMA bearish.
Above zero suggests upward movement with relative ease; below zero downward; use zero crosses and trend confirmation.
Above zero buyers dominate; below zero sellers dominate; divergence can warn of weakening trend.
Bullish on actual fast-above-slow crossover and alignment; bearish on reverse. 50/200 is long-term confirmation.
Calibrate width to volatility. Upper break can be strength, not automatic sell; use trend and reversal confirmation.
Fisher crossing above trigger is bullish; below trigger bearish. Treat extremes as reversal setups only.
Short group above and expanding away from long group is bullish; reverse is bearish; compression warns transition.
Compare current value with its 1-year percentile; rising means higher realized risk, not direction.
Close above a rising HMA is bullish; below a falling HMA bearish; slope change can flag transition.
Strong bullish: price above cloud, Tenkan above Kijun, bullish future cloud and Chikou confirmation; reverse bearish.
Upper-channel close can confirm strength; lower can confirm weakness. Mean reversion requires reversal and trend context.
KO crossing above signal is bullish and below bearish; zero-line position is secondary; monitor divergence.
KST above signal is bullish, especially above zero; below signal and zero is bearish.
Close above a rising LSMA is bullish; below a falling LSMA bearish.
Bullish when price is above a rising regression curve; bearish below a falling curve; slope is essential.
Positive slope bullish, negative bearish; larger absolute value means stronger trend. Normalize for cross-stock comparison.
Use actual crossover and alignment. Fast above slow is bullish; fast below slow bearish.
EMA above SMA with both rising is bullish; below with both falling bearish. Avoid equal 20/20 periods.
MACD above signal is bullish; above zero strengthens it. Use histogram direction for acceleration and watch divergence.

indicators.parameters: Family-weighted score; not equal indicator tally
indicators.rule: Aggregate normalized family scores to avoid double-counting correlated indicators. Suggested weights: Trend 30, Momentum 20, Volume 20, Volatility 10, Relative/Breadth 10, Structure 10.
Classic reversal bulge: rises above 27 then falls below 26.5. Predicts possible reversal, not direction.
Close above a rising McGinley line is bullish; below a falling line bearish.
Reference series only. Close above means upper half of range but is not a standalone buy.
Above zero and rising is bullish; below zero and falling bearish; divergence can warn of reversal.
Below 20 oversold and above 80 overbought. Require threshold re-cross, divergence or price confirmation; not automatic trades.
Close above a rising MA is bullish; 20>50>200 is strong alignment; reverse is bearish.
Close above a rising KAMA is bullish; below a falling KAMA bearish.
Close above upper channel is bullish breakout; below lower bearish. Do not use center MA alone.
Close above a rising DEMA bullish; below falling DEMA bearish.
Close above rising EMA bullish; 20>50>200 strong bullish alignment; reverse bearish.
Close above a rising Hamming MA is bullish; below a falling line bearish.
Shorter MAs ordered above longer MAs confirms bullish trend quality; compression indicates transition.
10>20>50 bullish; 10<20<50 bearish; mixed ordering neutral.
Close above a rising WMA is bullish; below a falling WMA bearish.

indicators.parameters: Daily up-volume minus down-volume; smooth/cumulate 5-20 days
indicators.rule: Positive and rising smoothed net volume supports buying pressure; negative and falling supports selling pressure.
Rising OBV confirms accumulation; falling confirms distribution; divergence against price is important.
Dots below price bullish and above bearish; use mainly in trends as trailing stop, not in choppy markets.
Above PP gives bullish bias and below bearish; use S1-S3/R1-R3 for confirmation, targets and invalidation.
Close above prior upper channel bullish; below prior lower channel bearish.
Above zero bullish and below bearish; prefer oscillator-signal crossover and clarify PPO versus absolute oscillator.
Rising PVT confirms price rise; falling confirms decline; divergence indicates weak participation.
Above zero positive momentum; below zero negative; use zero cross and slope, not level alone.

indicators.parameters: Stock price divided by benchmark price
indicators.rule: Rising ratio means outperformance; falling means underperformance. Name the benchmark explicitly.
Above 50 bullish regime and below 50 bearish. <30/>70 are conditions; require re-cross/divergence for reversal trades.
RVI crossing above signal bullish and below bearish; zero line is secondary confirmation.
Above 50 favors upside volatility and below 50 downside; >60 bullish and <40 bearish bias. Original direction was reversed.
Main above signal and zero is bullish; below signal and zero bearish; use exact platform formula.
Close above a rising SMMA bullish; below a falling SMMA bearish.
Rising spread indicates first instrument outperforming the second; falling indicates underperformance. High-low range is not generic spread.
Rising means higher dispersion/risk and falling means compression; compare with historical percentile. No direction.
Lower error means price follows the fitted trend closely; rising error means lower trend reliability.
Outside bands means statistical extension. Use regression slope plus re-entry or breakout confirmation.
Bullish when %K crosses above %D from below 20; bearish when %K crosses below %D from above 80.
Bullish crossover from below 0.2 and bearish crossover from above 0.8; confirm with trend because it is sensitive.
Price above green line is bullish and below red line bearish; use as trend filter/trailing stop.

indicators.parameters: Length 14 common; confirm exact platform implementation
indicators.rule: Use platform-specific scale, signal line and thresholds. Do not assume universal zero-line rules without formula verification.
Close above a rising TEMA is bullish; below a falling TEMA bearish.
TRIX above signal and zero bullish; below signal and zero bearish; divergence can warn of reversal.
TSI above signal and zero bullish; below signal and zero bearish; monitor divergence.
Input/reference series for VWAP, MFI and CCI. It is not a useful standalone buy/sell rule.
Below 30 and above 70 are conditions. Bullish on cross back above 30 or bullish divergence; bearish on reverse.
Compare with historical percentile and peers; measures realized risk, not direction.

indicators.parameters: Confirm platform formula; for fear use VIX/India VIX separately
indicators.rule: Do not equate automatically with ATR or market VIX. Interpret only after confirming the exact series/formula.
Rising value means increasing realized risk; non-directional.
Use platform-defined zero-trend estimator; do not substitute mean absolute daily move. Non-directional.
Breakout volume >1.5x average is meaningful and >2x strong; direction comes from price.
Above zero means short-term volume expansion; below zero contraction. Combine with price direction.
Analyze POC, VAH, VAL, HVNs and LVNs. Acceptance above POC/VAH may be bullish; rejection changes interpretation.
Analyze POC, VAH/VAL and nodes for the current visible window; results change when the window changes.
VI+ crossing above VI- bullish; VI- above VI+ bearish; widening spread strengthens the signal.

indicators.parameters: Session VWAP intraday; anchored VWAP for swing/event
indicators.rule: Price above VWAP gives bullish bias and below bearish; prefer acceptance/retest and volume confirmation.
Close above a rising VWMA bullish; below falling bearish. Compare with EMA to judge volume confirmation.
Bullish on cross back above -80; bearish on cross below -20. Extremes alone are not trades.
Lips>Teeth>Jaw with widening separation bullish; reverse bearish; intertwined lines mean no trend.
Bullish only when price breaks above the latest confirmed upper fractal; bearish below latest confirmed lower fractal.
Use confirmed legs for higher-high/higher-low structure. Latest leg repaints and must not be used predictively.
